sanskrit: āvatas te parāvataḥ parāvatas ta āvataḥ | ihaiva bhava mā nu gā mā pūrvān anu gā gatān asuṃ badhnāmi te dṛḍham ||
english: From near at hand and from afar, from afar and from near: remain here, do not go away; do not follow those who have gone before. I bind your life-breath firmly.

sanskrit: yat tvābhiceruḥ puruṣaḥ so yad aruṇo janaḥ | unmocana pramocane ubhe vācā vadāmi te ||
english: Whatever man has bewitched you — that reddish-complexioned person — the release and the full release: both I proclaim to you with my voice.

sanskrit: yad dudrohitha śepiṣe striyai puṃse acittyā | (…) ||
english: Whatever wrong you have done unwittingly against a woman or a man, against the reviled — [the release and the full release: both I proclaim to you with my voice].

sanskrit: yad enaso mātṛkṛtāc cheṣe pitṛkṛtād uta | unmocana pramocane ubhe vācā vadāmi te ||
english: Whatever sin you lie under, whether done by your mother or done by your father — the release and the full release: both I proclaim to you with my voice.

sanskrit: yat te mātā yat te pitā jāmir bhrātā ca sarjataḥ | pratyak sevasya bheṣajaṃ jaradaṣṭiṃ kṛṇomi tvā ||
english: What your mother, what your father, your sister and your brother have let loose — the healing of self-return: I make you one who lives to old age.

sanskrit: ehy ehi punar ehi sarveṇa manasā saha | dūtau yamasya mānu gā adhi jīvapurā ihi ||
english: Come, come, come back again, together with your whole mind. Do not follow the two messengers of Yama; enter instead into the city of the living.

sanskrit: anuhūtaḥ punar ehi vidvān udayanaṃ pathaḥ | ārohaṇam ākramaṇaṃ jīvatojīvato 'yanam ||
english: Called back, return again, knowing the upward path — the path of ascent, of forward stride, the way of the living, the living.

sanskrit: mā bibher na mariṣyasi jaradaṣṭir bhaviṣyasi | nir avocam ahaṃ yakṣmam aṅgebhyo aṅgajvaraṃ tava ||
english: Fear not — you shall not die; you shall come to be grasped by old age. I have driven away the yakṣma from your limbs, the fever-of-limbs that was yours.

sanskrit: śīrṣarogo aṅgarogo yaś ca te hṛdayāmayaḥ | yakṣmaḥ śyena iva prāpaptad vācā nuttaḥ parastaram ||
english: The head-disease, the body-disease, and whatever heart-ailment afflicts you — the yakṣma has flown far away like a hawk, driven off by the spoken word, to a place beyond.

sanskrit: ṛṣī bodhapratībodhāv asvapno yaś ca jāgṛviḥ | te te prāṇasya goptāro divā naktaṃ ca jāgratu ||
english: The two ṛṣis Bodha and Pratibodha, Non-sleep and Wakefulness — they are the guardians of your prāṇa; may they keep watch over you by day and by night.

sanskrit: ayam agnir upasadya iha sūrya ud etu te | ud ehi mṛtyor gambhīrāt kṛcchrāc cit tamasas pari ||
english: This Agni, having been duly approached, — may Sūrya rise here for you. Rise up out of the deep of death, even out of the grievous place, away from the darkness.

sanskrit: namo yamāya namo 'stu mṛtyave namaḥ pitṛbhya uta ye nayante | utpāraṇasya yo veda tam agniṃ tat puro dadhe ||
english: Homage to Yama, homage be to Mṛtyu, homage to the Pitṛs and to those who lead [the dead]. Him who knows the rite of crossing over — that Agni I set before [us] as the vanguard.

sanskrit: aitu prāṇa aitu mana aitu cakṣur atho balam | śarīram asya saṃ vidāṃ tat padbhyāṃ prati tiṣṭhatu ||
english: Let prāṇa come back; let mind come back; let sight come back, and strength. Let him be reunited with his body; let it stand firm upon its feet.

sanskrit: prāṇenāgne cakṣuṣā saṃ sṛjemaṃ sam īraya tanvā saṃ balena | vetthāmṛtasya mā mṛta mo ṣu bhūmigṛho bhuvat ||
english: O Agni, unite him with breath and with sight; stir him together with body and with strength. You know the immortal; let him not die — let him not become a dwelling of earth.

sanskrit: mā te prāṇa upa dasan māpāno api dhāyi te | sūryas tvādhipatir mṛtyor udāyacchāti raśmibhiḥ ||
english: Let your prāṇa not fail; let your apāna not be laid down. Sūrya, the sovereign over death, draws you upward with his rays.

sanskrit: iyam antar vadaty ugrā jihvā paniṣpadā | tayā rogān vi nayāmaḥ śataṃ ropīś ca takmanaḥ ||
english: This fierce tongue, jerking within, speaks out. With it we drive away the diseases — the hundred sores and the fever, takman.

sanskrit: ayaṃ lokaḥ priyatamo devānām aparājitaḥ | yasmai tvam iha jajñiṣe diṣṭaḥ puruṣa mṛtyave | tasmai tvānu hvayāmasi mā purā jaraso mṛthāḥ ||
english: This world, most dear to the gods, unconquered — for this you, O man, were born here, appointed to death. For this life we call you back: do not die before old age.

sanskrit: te 'vadan prathamā brahmakilbiṣe 'kūpāraḥ salilo mātariśvā | vīḍuharas tapa ugraṃ mayobhuva āpo devīḥ prathamajā ṛtasya ||
english: These first declared [the truth] concerning sin against brahman: Akūpāra, Salila, Mātariśvā, Vīḍuhara, the fierce heat, the bliss-bestowing — the divine waters, first-born of ṛta.

sanskrit: somo rājā prathamo brahmajāyāṃ punaḥ prāyacchad ahṛṇīyamānaḥ | anvartitā varuṇo mitra āsīd agnir hotā hastagṛhyā nināya ||
english: King Soma was the first to return the brahmin's wife, without anger. Varuṇa was the upholder, Mitra was present; Agni the hotr̥, taking her by the hand, led her away.

sanskrit: hasteneva grāhya ādhir asyā brahmajāyeti ced avocat | na dūtāya prahye tastha eṣā tathā rāṣṭraṃ gupitaṃ kṣatriyasya ||
english: Like something to be received hand-to-hand is the sacred deposit of her — provided he has said 'she is the brahmin's wife.' She is not to stand available for dispatch as a messenger; thus is the kingdom protected for the kṣatriya.

sanskrit: yām āhus tārakāṃ vikeśīṃ ducchunāṃ grāmam avapadyamānām | sā brahmajāyā pra dunoti rāṣṭraṃ yatra prāpādi śaśaḥ kalkuṣīmān ||
english: Her whom they call the falling star, the disheveled-haired, the ill-omened one descending upon the village — she, the brahmin's wife [wronged], devastates the kingdom; there the blemished hare has set foot.

sanskrit: brahmacārī carati veviṣad viṣaḥ sa devānāṃ bhavaty ekam aṅgam | tena jāyām anv avindad bṛhaspatiḥ somena nītāṃ juhvaṃ na devāḥ ||
english: The brahmacārin wanders, trembling, full of potent force; he becomes a single limb of the gods. With him Bṛhaspati recovered his wife who had been led away by Soma — as the gods [recover] the sacrificial ladle.

sanskrit: devā etasyām avadanta pūrve saptarṣayas tapase ye niṣeduḥ | bhīmā jāyā brāhmaṇasyāpanītā durdhāṃ dadhāti parame vyoman ||
english: The gods spoke of her in ancient times, as did the seven ṛṣis who sat themselves down for austerity: fearsome is the brahmin's wife when she has been carried away; she establishes his hardship in the highest vault of heaven.

sanskrit: ye garbhā avapadyante jagad yac cāpalupyate | vīrā ye hanyante mitho brahmajāyā hinasti tān ||
english: The foetuses that are miscarried, and whatever of the living world is plundered, the heroes who are slain in mutual strife — the brahmin's wife [when wronged] destroys all these.

sanskrit: sarve garbhāḥ pra vyathante kumārā daśamāsyāḥ | yasmin rāṣṭre nirudhyate brahmajāyā acittyā ||
english: All foetuses tremble and the ten-month children [in the womb] are shaken, in whatever kingdom the brahmin's wife is detained through thoughtlessness.

sanskrit: punar vai devā adaduḥ punar manuṣyā uta | rājānaḥ satyaṃ kṛṇvanto brahmajāyāṃ punar daduḥ ||
english: The gods indeed returned her again, and so too did men. Kings, acting according to truth, returned the brahmin's wife.

sanskrit: punardāya brahmajāyāṃ kṛtvī devair nikilbiṣam | ūrjaṃ pṛthivyā bhaktvā- -urugāyam upāsate ||
english: Having returned the brahmin's wife and having made themselves sinless before the gods, they attend upon the widely-praised [one], partaking of the vital nourishment of the earth.
